title: Industry 4.0
standfirst: IoT, cyber-physical systems and the data infrastructures behind the fourth industrial revolution.

description_paragraphs: This course introduces the key aspects of Industry 4.0, connects its challenges to relevant data science techniques, and develops tools and data-driven business models for real-world applications.
faculty: Prof. Rahul Marathe, Department of Management Studies, IIT Madras

weeks_text.label: Week 1
weeks_text.text: Industry 4.0 foundations; Evolution of industrial revolutions; Concepts and examples of modern industrial systems.

weeks_text.label: Week 2
weeks_text.text: Facility layout design; Types of layouts (process, product, fixed-position); Layout optimization.

weeks_text.label: Week 3
weeks_text.text: Facility location problems; Single and multi-facility models; Optimization approaches (median problems).

weeks_text.label: Week 4
weeks_text.text: Sourcing decisions; Supplier segmentation; Association rule mining (Apriori algorithm).

weeks_text.label: Week 5
weeks_text.text: Inventory management fundamentals; EOQ and newsvendor models; Dynamic inventory (Bellman equations).

weeks_text.label: Week 6
weeks_text.text: Stochastic inventory models; Value and policy iteration; Dynamic decision-making.

weeks_text.label: Week 7
weeks_text.text: Inventory management in supply networks; Material flow; Multi-stage and omni-channel systems.

weeks_text.label: Week 8
weeks_text.text: Industry 4.0 technologies; IoT; Time series forecasting; Predictive maintenance.

weeks_text.label: Week 9
weeks_text.text: Logistics and distribution management; Transportation models; TSP and vehicle routing problems.

weeks_text.label: Week 10
weeks_text.text: Digital transformation; Industry 4.0 in manufacturing; Simulation, ERP , and digital twins.

weeks_text.label: Week 11
weeks_text.text: Pricing strategies; Capacity allocation; Revenue management (Littlewood's rule).

weeks_text.label: Week 12
weeks_text.text: AI applications in manufacturing; Intelligent and automated production systems.
